mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 130 D300 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt DT306 engine for the Land Rover Defender 130 D300 typically costs £8,000-£12,000 supply-only through our specialist network, while reconditioned units start around £6,500 and used engines from £4,000. Supply and fit packages add labour on top, but remain significantly cheaper than main dealer pricing.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing DT306 engine in a Land Rover Defender 130 D300?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warnings in the Land Rover Defender 130 D300 are unexplained coolant loss, a distinct rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold starts (timing chain rattle), or illuminated DPF and temperature warning lights. You should also watch for white exhaust smoke or oil residue around the EGR assembly.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Land Rover Defender 130 D300?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A typical Land Rover Defender 130 D300 holds a UK market value of £60,000-£85,000+, making an £8,000-£12,000 rebuilt engine a financially sound investment that preserves the vehicle's performance, reliability and strong resale value for years to come.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 130 D300 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Land Rover Defender 130 D300 typically takes 3-5 days depending on specialist workload and whether ancillary components such as the EGR or cooling system are being upgraded at the same time. Sourcing a quality rebuilt DT306 unit may add a few days.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Land Rover Defender 130 D300 and the P400 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Land Rover Defender 130 D300 uses a 3.0-litre inline-6 mild-hybrid diesel engine (DT306/AJ20D6) producing 300 PS and 650 Nm of torque, prioritising low-end pulling power and fuel efficiency for towing. In contrast, the P400 uses a 3.0-litre inline-6 mild-hybrid petrol engine producing 400 PS, focused on higher-revving performance and refinement.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Defender 130 D300 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 3.0-litre Ingenium inline-six diesel (DT306/AJ20D6) in the Land Rover Defender 130 D300 is a refined and capable powerplant, but early examples have shown susceptibility to timing chain and EGR system wear. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Land Rover Defender 130 D300 DT306 Develops a Rattle
problems.rootCause: The hydraulic timing chain tensioner can lose pressure over time, allowing the chain to stretch and produce a characteristic rattle on cold starts. If ignored, this can lead to catastrophic internal engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip front covers, replace timing chain, guides and updated tensioner assembly.
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive fix for chain rattle; prevents catastrophic valve-to-piston contact if addressed promptly.

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £8,000-£12,000 [ESTIMATED - using Land Rover 306DT as proxy for 3.0L diesel]
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply and fit of a rebuilt DT306 with upgraded valvetrain components, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended only if chain failure has already caused internal engine damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Land Rover Defender 130 D300 of relevant age (2022-present) currently holds a UK market value of approximately £60,000-£85,000+ [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader / Cazoo market observations]. At this premium value band, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine replacement is a small fraction of the vehicle's worth and easily justifies the investment to preserve performance and resale value.
problems.recommendation: Do not ignore a cold-start rattle in your Land Rover Defender 130 D300. A timely chain and tensioner replacement by a specialist is a well-documented fix that preserves the engine's longevity at a fraction of the cost of a full rebuild.

problems.group: EGR Cooler Leaks & DPF Regeneration Issues
problems.h4: EGR Cooler Leaks & DPF Regeneration Issues - Why the Land Rover Defender 130 D300 DT306 Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can develop internal or external leaks under sustained thermal cycling, leading to unexplained coolant loss and potential DPF contamination if left unaddressed.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and replace the EGR cooler assembly, flush the cooling system and update software.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective if caught before overheating or severe DPF contamination occurs.

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £8,000-£12,000 [ESTIMATED - using Land Rover 306DT as proxy for 3.0L diesel]
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply and fit of a rebuilt DT306 with upgraded cooling components, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the engine has already suffered thermal damage or severe internal contamination.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above, the £60,000-£85,000+ value of a Land Rover Defender 130 D300 makes targeted repairs like an EGR cooler refresh a straightforward investment. Full replacement is rarely justified for minor seepage alone unless secondary damage has occurred.
problems.recommendation: If your Land Rover Defender 130 D300 is showing minor coolant loss or DPF warning lights but has not overheated, a targeted EGR cooler refresh is the most cost-effective route and can extend the engine's life significantly.
